$comment: Riftlight, Restless Coast arrival (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, saltrot-arrival; design note saltrot-arrival-review.md). Revised in November 2026 for the campaign rewrite: the checks, fight, Attune lesson (gated on attune_taught) and arrival variants are kept. Question: why is glacier silt on a mudflat? Puddle, the Skupper guide, is introduced and carries it; Pip Thistledown is introduced in words true whether or not the party has met him. Sets attune_taught; reads saltrot_arrival_* and glacier_rift_woken.
title: Mud Where Ice Should Be

goal.text: Why is glacier silt on a mudflat?

steps.label: Dig out a buried front door
Find where the cold silt comes from
Get everyone past the early tide

plate.narration: Gray-green mudflats stretch toward a hazy sea. Silt banks, salt pools and crooked drowned trees. Out here the ground changes its mind with every tide.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. Nobody dies.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.saltrot_guide: Puddle, the Skupper guide (she/her). Quick, chatty and cheerfully blunt. Guides from brackish pools and channels and signals with her tall crest; puffs up round when startled, and stings a little. Fits exactly in a puddle, hence the name. Keeps her lunch in a floating box. Wants her town's door open and to find out why her flats keep moving, so Grandmother Winkle will trust her paths.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, pries things with a spoon, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants to impress her.
npcVoices.Grandmother Winkle: Puddle's grandmother (she/her), a strict old Skupper guide. Short words, big frown, kind underneath. Keeps the guides' rule: show the bank, never the stone.
npcVoices.Dab: A small Skupper child (she/her). Licks things to learn about them. Puffs up when startled.
npcVoices.Fen: A frogfolk fisher (she/her). Brisk, practical, always carrying a fish bag the gulls follow.
npcVoices.Old Ossley: Frogfolk ferryman (he/him). Slow, dry and kind. "I'm your frog."
npcVoices.Seren Wisp: Kitsune Riftseeker (she/her). Calm and quiet; listens before she speaks.

flats.narration: Brackish water curls around ridges of mud. A Skupper pops up in a puddle exactly her size, crest high. "Puddle!" she says. "Your guide. Named for the puddle. There's always one that fits." She points a fin at a heap of pale, cold silt. "My town's front door is under that. Saltrot mud is brown and warm. This is gray, like glacier ice ground to flour. What's glacier silt doing on my mudflat?"

variants.text: Behind you, Old Ossley poles his flat boat back into the channel.
Behind you, the fold still hums with cold glacier air.
Behind you, the linked fold carries the cloud whales' distant song.

shells.narration: Puddle skips ahead, pool to pool. "I need water. You need shells. Mud has opinions," she says. "Skip where I skip, or poke before you step." Fiddler crabs wave one big claw each, in rows, like a crowd at a parade.

shells_a_check.narration: One big hop, two small ones, one wobble. A fiddler crab waves at every hop. Puddle says it is counting. Counting what, she won't say.
shells_a_check.prompt: Skip along in Puddle's footprints. Light feet, and no stopping!

onSuccess.narration: Dry-ish boots, all of you. "Good skipping," says Puddle. From a Skupper, that is a medal.

shells_b_check.narration: Puddle hands you a long reed pole. Poke, listen for the squelch, then step. Where the pole sinks, go around.
shells_b_check.prompt: Poke, listen and pick the firmest shells to step on

onSuccess.narration: Poke, squelch, step. You never sink once. Puddle tries very hard not to look impressed.

shells_off.narration: One leg sinks to the knee with a long, rude squelch. Puddle tows you out by the sleeve, and your shin stings where a shell scraped it. The mud keeps your sock. "Mud likes socks," says Puddle. "It's starting a collection."

shell_path.narration: The last steps up are three kinds of shell: whelk, cockle and oyster. "Wrong order, and they roll," says Puddle. She whispers a different bit of the order to each of you. "Put it together. I'm a guide, not a parrot."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then step on the shells in order.
clues: Puddle says: start on the whelk.
The oyster comes last, because it is the biggest.
The cockle is somewhere in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: Whelk, cockle, oyster. Every shell holds, and you are up in no time.

onFailure.narration: A shell rolls. You slide back to the bottom and climb again the long way, which takes ages. "Scenic route," says Puddle, not laughing.

onAssisted.narration: You lay the clues side by side, and the order is clear. Up you go.

town.narration: A round hatch in the mud is the front door of Tidepocket, Puddle's burrow town. Cold gray silt is piled on it like icing. Tap, tap, TAP comes from below. "Grandmother Winkle," says Puddle. "Strict. She says a guide who can't clear her own door can't keep anybody's path." Puddle's crest droops. "Help me dig?"

variants.text: The tide is already licking the hatch. No time for clever plans.

town_a_check.narration: Everyone grabs a shell scoop. Puddle digs too, flinging silt over her shoulder and onto your boots. "Sorry. Sorry. Not sorry, dig!"
town_a_check.prompt: Dig until the hatch pops free!

town_b_check.narration: Puddle draws a line in the mud with one fin. "Water runs downhill. Make it carry the silt away for us."
town_b_check.prompt: Plan a trench so the silt slides away, not back onto the hatch

onSuccess.narration: The trench drinks the silt like soup.

town_brace.narration: Your thornguard plants both feet and braces the sagging hatch frame, so the silt can't slump back. Puddle digs between those sturdy legs. "Best fence I ever had," she says.

town_brace_check.narration: The frame holds. Now the silt only has one way to go: out.
town_brace_check.prompt: Dig hard while your thornguard holds the frame steady

town_done.narration: The hatch swings up with a pop and a puff of warm air. Skuppers pour out in a cheerful line, blinking. Last comes a very small, very old Skupper with a very large frown: Grandmother Winkle. "About time," she says. Then she sees the clean hatch, and almost smiles.

town_off.narration: The silt slumps back over half the hatch. A Skupper child pops out through the gap like a cork, then another. At last Grandmother Winkle squeezes out sideways, muddy to the crest. "Half a door," she says, and looks at Puddle. Puddle looks at her feet.

hatch_party.narration: The whole town blinks in the sunlight, and everybody wants help at once. "Pick a job," says Puddle, "and do it loudly." Grandmother Winkle supervises from a shell, which mostly means pointing.

interaction.cue: Everyone pick a job and help the families out.

options.label: Hand out kelp cakes
options.reaction: A small Skupper takes a cake in each fin and another in her mouth.

options.label: Sweep silt off the steps
options.reaction: The steps shine. A crab inspects them and approves.

options.label: Cheer for Grandmother Winkle
options.reaction: Grandmother Winkle says "About time" again, but she waves.

stages: The steps are clear and the cakes are going around.

silt.narration: Now you can see the silt properly. It is pale and gray and cold, like flour left out in the snow. "Saltrot mud is warm," says Puddle. "This came from somewhere with ice." A Skupper child named Dab licks some. "Tastes like old pennies." Nobody asks how Dab knows what pennies taste like.

local.narration: "The silt buried my path markers overnight," says Puddle. On a far shell-bank, a frogfolk fisher named Fen hops on one foot as the water rises. Her fish bag sits on the next bank, and the gulls have noticed. "She followed my markers," Puddle groans, "and they went the wrong way." "Help me get my bag?" calls Fen.

choices.label: Pass the bag along a line

bag_check.narration: You line up shell to shell, ready to pass the bag. It smells very strongly of fish. The gulls are extremely interested.
bag_check.prompt: Pass the bag hand to hand without stepping off the firm shells

onSuccess.narration: Hand, hand, hand, and the bag arrives dry. A gull lands on your head in protest.

path_check.narration: Puddle hands you empty shells. "Firm ground only. Trust a path once, then look again."
path_check.prompt: Pick the firmest shells and lay a path Fen can follow

onSuccess.narration: Fen hops along your new markers, grabs her bag, and hops back. "Now that's a path," she says. Puddle's crest stands up tall.

traveler_done.narration: Fen hugs her bag and gives you a dried fish, which nobody will be eating, and a small river charm. "For luck on soft ground. It warms up over firm mud." She squelches off, gulls following in a hopeful cloud.

traveler_off.narration: A wave slaps the bank and soaks the bag. Fen grabs it herself, dripping. "Mostly dry. Mostly." She squelches off without saying thank you, and Puddle scratches a note in the mud with one fin: look again.

puff.narration: Something round bobs past in the channel. It's Dab, puffed up three times her size, spines out like a very round hedgehog. A gull startled her. Now she is floating toward deep water. "Puffed Skuppers float," says Puddle, her own crest straight up. "They can't steer!"

choices.label: Tow her in with a rope

puff_a.narration: Dab spins slowly in the current. Her tail fin pokes out behind her like a little handle.
puff_a.prompt: Throw the rope loop around Dab's tail fin and tow her in. Mind the spines!

puff_b.narration: "Low and slow," whispers Puddle. "Like the tide going out."
puff_b.prompt: Hum a slow, calm tune until Dab lets her breath out

puff_song.narration: Your songkeeper sings a slow song about the tide going out. Dab's spines droop, little by little.
puff_song.prompt: Sing the tide song softly and keep Dab calm until she shrinks

puff_done.narration: Dab lets out a squeaky sigh and shrinks, like a small round bagpipe. "Thanks. This morning I saw old stone posts upriver, where the pale silt starts. And it was snowing on them. Just on them." Puddle goes quiet. Grandmother Winkle sends a warm honeycake after you, for saving Dab.

puff_off.narration: Dab drifts out of reach. Puddle dives in, tows her back, and gets a spine in the nose for her trouble. So do you, pulling them both out. "Ow. Family," says Puddle. Dab sniffs. "Sorry. This morning I saw old stone posts upriver, where the pale silt starts. And it was snowing on them. Just on them."

ossley.narration: A flat boat runs aground with a soft thump. Old Ossley, the frogfolk ferryman, peers over the side, his boat full of crates for Tidepocket. "It's this cold silt," he grumbles. "Never had it down here till this season. Came down the river with the melt. Hands?"

variants.text: He winks at you. "Same river, same fare, eh?"

ossley_a.narration: The crates are heavy and smell of kelp. Ossley hums a rowing song to keep the time.
ossley_a.prompt: Make a chain and pass the crates ashore before the tide climbs

ossley_b.narration: "Under the keel," says Ossley, "and lift where she's flat."
ossley_b.prompt: Slide planks under the keel so the boat floats free

ossley_done.narration: The boat floats free. Ossley catches a sliding crate of kelp with his tongue, without looking. "Honest work, honest pay." He pays you five coins. "When you want to go upriver, I'm your frog."

ossley_off.narration: The tide wins the race. You carry the last crates through knee-deep water while Ossley bails with a bucket. Two crates arrive damp. "For the wet ones," he says, and pays you three coins, not five. "When you want to go upriver, I'm your frog."

camp.narration: The families press a hot kelp cake into every hand. "Diggers eat first," says Puddle, and eats first anyway. Grandmother Winkle settles on her shell. Out on the flats, two travelers are wading toward the town's lamps.

choices.label: Ask Grandmother Winkle about the silt

camp_story.narration: "Silt comes from where water comes from," says Grandmother Winkle. "Upriver is a bridge with no river. Guides have one rule for it: show the bank, never the stone." She squints at Puddle. "You know the rule?" "Yes, Grandmother." Then she tells it again, shorter.

variants.text: "And a guide," she adds, "finishes digging her own door." Puddle's crest droops.

camp_gift.narration: Grandmother Winkle breaks the honeycake into tiny pieces and keeps the smallest. "Good manners. Upriver is a bridge with no river. Guides have one rule for it: show the bank, never the stone." She taps Puddle's crest. "You may show these ones the bank." Puddle's crest shoots straight up.

lesson.narration: Seren Wisp, the kitsune from the glacier, has come down the river with Pip Thistledown, a young manticore scout with a notebook and a spoon he pries things with. Pip waves the spoon at you like an old friend. He waves it at everybody. "Every rift hums," says Seren. "A starweaver can learn to answer one. That is called Attune." Far off, something hums like a bee in a bucket. "Lady Olivia says knock loud!" says Pip.

variants.text: Seren Wisp has come down the river with Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, checking another place that has moved. Pip waves his spoon at you. He waves it at everybody. Far off, something hums like a bee in a bucket. Seren asks you to listen and compare it with what she taught you before. "Lady Olivia says knock loud!" says Pip.

choices.label: Hum the hall note and listen
Walk and mark the quiet spots

hum_a_check.narration: You hum low together. Puddle hums too, loudly and a little flat. Then everyone holds still.
hum_a_check.prompt: Hum the hall note, then hold still and listen for the flats to hum back

hum_b_check.narration: Pip hands out shells to mark the spots. The hum fades, and grows, and fades.
hum_b_check.prompt: Walk the flats and mark every spot where the hum goes quiet

hum_chime.narration: You ring the Listening Chime near the mud, softly. The note rises, then bends, as if something far away answered in a slightly different voice.
hum_chime.prompt: Follow the bend in the chime's note across the flats

hum_star.narration: Your starweaver listens the way Seren taught, and the flats hum a little louder in answer. Everyone else keeps still.
hum_star.prompt: Answer the hum with Attune, and follow it across the mud

hum_done.narration: Under the mud, a low note hums back from far to the north. In your pack, the Listening Chime leans that way all by itself, north and up the river, toward the glacier. Seren goes very still. Pip writes GLACIER and underlines it twice. Puddle's crest folds flat. "The silt comes from the ice," she whispers. "From your ice."

hum_off.narration: The hum hides in the squelch, so Pip knocks your chime with his spoon. BONG. Every fiddler crab dives into its hole, and something under the silt grumbles. But far to the north, a low note answers, and the chime leans that way, toward the glacier. "The silt comes from the ice," Puddle whispers. "From your ice."

trail.narration: Pip spreads his muddy map on a reed drum. The pale stripe of silt runs upriver, wider and colder the farther it goes. "Follow it, and we find where it starts!" Seren asks Puddle to come. Puddle folds her fins. "To the high shells. Not past them. Past them is the old bank, and Grandmother's rule."

trail_a_check.narration: Brown mud on one side, gray silt on the other. The gray part is cold enough to make your toes curl.
trail_a_check.prompt: Keep one foot on each color of mud, and do not lose the stripe

trail_b_check.narration: "Poke the gray," says Puddle. "It's softer than it looks."
trail_b_check.prompt: Work out where firm ground ends and soft silt begins

trail_charm_check.narration: Fen's river charm warms over firm mud and goes cool over soft. Puddle decides not to be offended that a pebble is better at her job.
trail_charm_check.prompt: Follow the charm along the stripe: warm for firm, cool for soft

trail_wing_check.narration: A winged friend rises over the flats and follows the pale stripe like a gray ribbon.
trail_wing_check.prompt: Fly along the stripe and call the way down to the walkers

trail_done.narration: The pale stripe grows wider and colder, a gray road through the brown. Ahead, it climbs a long, low rise. Pip skips ahead, notebook out. "Lady Olivia will want a map of this!" Behind you, every fiddler crab lifts its claw at once.

trail_off.narration: You lose the stripe twice under fresh brown mud and find it again by falling into it. Your knee is not happy. Pip helps you up, and his spoon helps nobody. Behind you, every fiddler crab lifts its claw at once.

crabs.narration: The crabs wave together, all facing upriver. "They don't do that," says Puddle. "They wave by the tide, and the tide's hours away." Her crest shoots up. "They know something we don't. Find out. Fast."

choices.label: Time the waves against a pole

crabs_a.narration: Wave, wave, wave. The water mark on the pole creeps down when it should creep up.
crabs_a.prompt: Count the waves and read the water mark. What are the crabs telling you?

crabs_b.narration: The rise is slick gray silt all the way up. Pip goes first and slides past you on his way back down.
crabs_b.prompt: Scramble up the slippery rise before the next wave of crabs

crabs_leap_check.narration: Your manticore crouches, wiggles and leaps high onto the ledge in one bound. Pip's mouth falls open. "Teach me that!"
crabs_leap_check.prompt: Leap to the ledge, look upriver and call down what you see

crabs_done.narration: Upriver, water is piling up behind a long gray bar of silt, like a bath with the plug in. "When that bar gives, the water comes all at once," you tell Puddle. "An early tide," she says. "But that's not what they're waving about." The silt beside you heaves.

crabs_off.narration: You work it out late, after a crab pinches your toe to hurry you up. Upriver, water is piling up behind a long gray bar of silt. "An early tide," says Puddle. "But that's not why they're waving." The silt beside you heaves.

crab_warn.narration: Two big crabs push up out of the silt, shells clear as windows. "Glassback crabs," whispers Puddle. "The cold silt froze their warm mud. Now they want this warm bank." "Lady Olivia says stand your ground!" says Pip. "Or we find them somewhere warmer," says Puddle. "That takes time, and the tide is coming."

variants.text: Pip's BONG woke them early, and they are too cross to follow anybody.

crab_fight.narration: The crabs want your warm shell-bank. Keep a hero on its marked hollow for two round ends while the others draw them aside. The cold silt starts slumping in round two. Cross it if you must, but stopping there costs steps next turn. The tide will not wait forever.

variants.text: You keep the hollow clear while Puddle braces its edge with shells. The crabs give up trying to squeeze you off it.

crab_done.narration: The crabs back off, glaring, and scuttle away over the flats. One leaves a glassy pebble at your feet. "A luckstone," says Puddle. "Very good manners, for a crab." Then she frowns after them. "They're still cold. They'll be at somebody's door by the next tide." Behind you, water begins to slide.

crab_rescued.narration: A crab shoves you off the bank, and you sit down in cold silt. Far off, the Tidepocket families bang cooking pots, and the crabs back away and squat on the warm bank, grumbling. It is theirs now, and it was the quick way up. Behind you, water begins to slide.

crab_lead.narration: Puddle sniffs the air. "Warm mud smells like toast. Find the toast."
crab_lead.prompt: Find a warm hollow and coax the crabs into it, one sideways step at a time

crab_led.narration: You find a hollow where the sun has sat all day. The crabs sink in up to their eyes and sigh like kettles. "They'll stay," says Puddle, proud. "No more crabs at anybody's door." Then she looks upriver. "But that took a while." Behind you, water begins to slide.

crab_nipped.narration: You find a warm hollow, but the crabs take the long way to it, right through your ankles. Pinch. Pinch. At last they sink in and sigh like kettles. "They'll stay," says Puddle. "Your ankles will recover." Then she looks upriver. "But that took a while." Behind you, water begins to slide.

tide.narration: Up the channel, the silt bar gives way. A gray wall of water slides toward you, quiet as a cat. For the first time, Puddle sounds worried. "High shells! Now!"

variants.text: The quick way up is the warm bank, and the crabs are sitting on it. You'll have to wade.
You spent the quiet minutes on the crabs. The water is already at your knees. No running now.

choices.label: Wade across in a rope chain

tide_a.narration: "Light and fast!" calls Puddle, swimming beside you. "Don't stop to look at it!"
tide_a.prompt: Run for the high shells and beat the water!

tide_b.narration: Pip ties the rope to his own tail, then thinks better of it. The water is cold, and it pulls.
tide_b.prompt: Anchor the rope on a firm shell and hold it while everyone wades along

tide_done.narration: Everyone's across, and Pip counts heads twice. "Right number," he says. A fiddler crab is sitting on his head, waving. One last channel lies between you and the high shells, and the water breathes in and out.

tide_off.narration: The water knocks your feet away and fills your boots, cold as a river from the north, which is exactly what it is. Everyone stays together, soggy and safe. Pip wrings out his map. Puddle wrings out Pip. One last channel lies ahead.

tide_dash.narration: The water pulls back from the last channel, then rushes in again, like a giant, rude breath. "Wait for the pull," says Puddle, crest raised high. "Then go."

interaction.cue: Go when the water pulls back.

onSuccess.narration: You hop across on dry shells to the high shells. Puddle cheers like it's a race.

onFailure.narration: The water grabs you mid-hop. Puddle puffs up round, and you ride the last bit on her like a spiky raft. "Ow. You're welcome."

onAssisted.narration: Puddle drops her crest on each pull, and you all cross on the last one.

lead.narration: From the high shells you see where the pale stripe ends: a line of old stone arches, standing in dry ground with no river under them. A little snow is falling on them, and only on them. "The buried bridge," Puddle says quietly. "Show the bank, never the stone." Seren looks north, toward the white mountains. "Master Orin Vale studies silt. He should see this."

choices.label: Sit with Puddle as the tide goes out

ending.narration: The water goes back out, slow and silver. Puddle scratches the day into the mud for the guides' account. "Tomorrow I'll show you the bank of the buried bridge. The bank. Not the stone." So here is your piece: the cold silt burying this town came down the river from the glacier. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: The glassback crabs doze in their warm hollow.
Somewhere, two cold glassback crabs are looking for a door to sit on.
The glassback crabs still squat on the warm bank, glaring.
Tidepocket's door stands clear, glowing like a pot of honey.
Half of Tidepocket's door is still under silt, and Grandmother Winkle is watching.
Grandmother Winkle said Puddle may show you the bank. Puddle keeps saying so.
The open fold still hums nearby. It could carry you back to the glacier.
